newsitem.title: USA: Dunavant sees 96/97 world cotton at 86.3 mln bales.
newsitem.headline: Dunavant sees 96/97 world cotton at 86.3 mln bales.

text.p: Leading cotton merchant William B. Dunavant Jr. pegged 1996/97 world cotton production at 86.3 million bales.
The USDA in its December supply/demand report put 1996/97 world output at 85.93 million bales. The USDA will release its January report on Friday.
He put 1996/97 world consumption at 84.3 million bales.
Dunavant said 1996/97 ending world carryover will be 36 million bales versus the USDA December estimate of 36.96 million bales.
He said China will import 2.1 million bales in 1996/97 of which 1.025 million will be from the U.S. Currently the U.S. 728,000 bales registered on sales to China.
Domestic consumption will rise to 11.1 million bales and exports will rise to nearly 6.9 million bales in 1996/97, for a total offtake 18 million bales, Dunavant said.
